A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ExeCoder. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ExeCoder evaluation on TransCoder-test-X, comparisons with eight LLM baselines, and representation and training-stage ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds representation-order and mixed-training experiments in Appendix A, Table 8.

M1.justification: The proposed method retains natural-language functional descriptions, textual AST and DFG encodings, and four-stage PERL fine-tuning. The alternative training orders in v3 are experimental controls, not changes to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use approximately 55K XLCoST-Instruct training instances and evaluate translation among C++, Python, and Java on TransCoder-test-X. The dataset construction and represented tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The eight external LLM baselines remain unchanged. v3 Appendix A additionally evaluates five alternative representation orders and a single-stage mixed-training comparator named Shuffle against the original PERL configuration.

E3.justification: The new Appendix A experiments introduce representation-order permutations and single-stage mixed training as controlled experimental conditions. Existing evaluation metrics, benchmark construction, and reported fine-tuning hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a systematic comparison of all six representation orders and mixed training in Appendix A. This directly tests the choice of staging and curriculum order, extending v1's analyses of individual representations and successive stages of the prescribed curriculum.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new ablation continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: All eight original result tables retain their numerical values after matching locations and numbering. New Table 8 reports average TCA of 81.473–82.650 for alternative orders and 82.173 for Shuffle, alongside the unchanged ExeCoder value of 83.035. These are additional control results, not an improvement in ExeCoder's reported performance.

T1.justification: The representation descriptions and metric definitions are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations; v3's additional curriculum study is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: executability representations, PERL, TransCoder-test-X, and claimed superiority over the evaluated LLMs. The headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit limitation that lengthy static-analysis representations increase fine-tuning costs and constrain scalability. Appendix A also interprets the new comparisons as supporting the prescribed curriculum, which achieves the best reported averages but does not win every individual translation direction.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the project-website pointer with an explicit code-access link. Existing training hyperparameters, prompts, representation construction, and deduplication instructions are retained; the implementation paragraph moves to Appendix C without changing its settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds introductory citations to Lu et al. (2025, AXIS) and Mei et al. (2025, a1), and removes Haldar and Hockenmaier (2024) with the sentence about generating functional descriptions using external LLMs. The main research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence are retained. v3 condenses several explanations, particularly AST encoding, reorganizes the appendices, moves implementation details, adds a Limitations section, and updates author information.

P2.justification: The document receives a global template and typography change, including the title block, headers, spacing, and caption placement. Figure 1 moves to the first page, the match-based table moves to Appendix B, several appendix displays are regrouped, and a new ablation table is added. Existing diagram content is retained.

improvement.justification: The new order and mixed-training controls provide more direct evidence for PERL's curriculum design than v1's stagewise comparisons alone. The explicit cost and scalability limitation also improves qualification of the method. These are useful but limited gains: the main empirical results remain unchanged, and the added comparisons still lack repeated-run and uncertainty reporting.
